answers.explanation: It climbs the hierarchy toward the CPU.
Until it's written back, the register's copy differs from the cache, memory, and disk copies.
Using a stale copy would give wrong results.
Cache coherency invalidates or updates other CPUs' copies when one CPU writes.
One CPU's update makes another CPU's cached copy stale.
It has to be fast, so the hardware handles it.
Replicas on separate machines must be kept consistent over a network that can be slow or broken.
